feedback: If a learner expects a card for every column in 706, show that leaving the tens place empty is exactly what the 0 records.
If the overlay is misaligned, align the right-hand edges so ones sit over ones and the hidden zeros line up under the larger cards.
activities.intendedInsight: The expanded form and the compact numeral are two views of the same number; the trailing zeros inside 300 and 60 are hidden when cards overlap, and a missing card leaves a placeholder 0.
learnerActions: Take place-value (arrow) cards 300, 60 and 2 and overlay them so the smaller cards cover the trailing zeros of the larger, forming 362.
Pull the cards apart to recover the expanded form 300 + 60 + 2.
Repeat with a number containing an internal zero: overlay 700 and 6 to form 706, and notice no tens card is used — the tens place stays 0.
Say which zeros were hidden under which cards.
activities.title: Arrow/place-value cards: overlay and pull apart

feedback: If the explanation only restates '706 is bigger', prompt back to the empty tens column and the value each digit holds.
Accept explanations that name an empty place being held, e.g. 'there are no tens, but the tens place must still be shown.'
activities.intendedInsight: Articulating why a placeholder is needed consolidates the idea and surfaces whether the learner truly treats 0 as marking an empty place.
learnerActions: A character keeps 'losing the zero' and reads 706 as 76.
Explain to the character what the 0 is doing and why 706 and 76 are different numbers.
Challenge the character with your own trap, e.g. ask how 350 differs from 35.
activities.title: Place-value detective: explain the zero
